utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-95-16-T, the Prosecutor versus Zoran Kupreskic, Mirjan Kupreskic, Vlatko Kupreskic, Drago Josipovic, Dragan Papic and Vladimir Santic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning. I gather we start with a character witness for Mr. Josipovic. Mrs. Milica Vukadinovic, could you please stand and make the solemn declaration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Counsel Susak.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I should also like to inform you that I have given up Slavica Cickovic who was the second character witness, because I went along with the advice of the Chamber. The statement -- the testimonies of these two witnesses would overlap, in fact, and I decided that this one witness would be enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Good morning, Mrs. Vukadinovic.

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Could you please tell the court your name, where do you work, who do you live with, where do you live?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: I'm Milica Vukadinovic. I live with my three children, underage. At present I work for Herzegovina Osiguranje, which is an insurance company in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Before you got that job where did you work before that? Will you please list all the jobs that you held as of 1991?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Since 1983 I worked for Sintevit, socially owned company until '92. In '92 I went to work for the police station in Vitez and I was there until '94. In 1994 I was appointed the holder of the health centre in Vitez. Then in 1994, to this day, I've been working as the head of the subsidiary of Herzegovina Osiguranje, which is Herzegovina insurance.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You worked for this Sintevit company in Vitez. Was Drago Josipovic also working there?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Drago Josipovic worked for the same company, Sintevit. He worked there at the same time as I did or, rather, he worked there before me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Do you know Drago Josipovic only from work or have you socialised outside work?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: I know Drago Josipovic both from work and privately.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Could you tell us what was his attitude toward work at the Sintevit?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: His attitude to work, he was an exemplary worker. He always performed all his duties in an exemplary manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: In other words, he did --

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: he was very industrious, never any disciplinary sanctions were taken against him. He was always regularly at his job, attended his workplace regularly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So he was an exemplary worker?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Were both Muslims and Croats employed by the Sintevit?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In our company there were about 300 people employed. There were Muslims and Croats and Serbs. On the average, about 80 per cent --

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Will you please slow down because of the interpreters?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: On the average, about 80 per cent were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And you mean about 20 per cent Croats and Serbs, is that so?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Croats and Serbs, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Will you tell us was Drago Josipovic involved in some other activities but work?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, he was a trade unionist. He was appointed there. He was a member of the commission for labour relations, and he was also a member of the Workers' Council. Those were the self-managment bodies under the then system.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Was he also the chairman of the executive board of the union?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was also the vice-chairman and the chairman. Subsequently there was also the action conference which covered three enterprises and he was also a member of the action conference.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. President, may I ask the usher to show this document to the witness, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: This is a certificate. Is it authentic? It was signed by the general manager.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could it be placed on the ELMO for the interpreters, please? Could it be placed on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: It says Vitezit-- would you please read it out? Do you think this is correct, that Drago Josipovic was engaged in all these activities?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I fully corroborate this certificate, which is also duly stamped. Yes, Drago Josipovic did perform all these duties in the company.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is D39/4.

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't get the first word.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: No. It's all right. Now, you told us that he was a very industrious worker. On what terms was he with his Muslim fellow workers?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Very correct. Most of the Muslims would say -- said that he was a moderate man and nominated him for all these activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You mean all these fora?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They believed he would take adequate decisions, I mean, in terms of improving the working conditions and the organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You told us that about 80 per cent of the employees were Muslims in that enterprise. What does that mean then if he was elected to all these fora by all these Muslims?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it means that they appreciated him highly and that he was a part of the normal -- of the regular life that we led there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You told us briefly how Drago Josipovic was at work, but I also asked you if you knew him off of the working hours and you told us you did. Do you know where his house is?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: I do. It is in the hamlet of Santici.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Do you know who else is in this house?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Drago Josipovic lived with his mother, with his wife and two children.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: What did his mother look like?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: His mother was very old. She recently died.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Was she healthy?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, in terms of health, like any person of advanced age, but she was at home. She led a regular life.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did Drago Josipovic have something to do with children who went to school?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. We talked about that often. He did take care of his children, of his family, of his home.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did he spend most of the time at home or outside? I mean, he had two children.

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Drago did take care of his children, and by large, he spent his time at home or around home.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did he perhaps have a house garden or something like that, or some livestock?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He does have a house with a small house garden. They have a small farm, and they also had a cow, some hens, and such like, and a vegetable garden.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So you said that he looked after his two minor children who went to school. What kind of care did he is show for his children, from what you saw?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, he saw that they would have a meal after they came from school. He helped their mother cook meals for them. He was there to meet them after school. He saw that they changed clothes and other things that had to do with children.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: What was the attitude of Drago Josipovic and his family towards the Muslims who are his neighbours?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I also know that. They were very considerate, and Drago even recommended his neighbour Islam Ahmic to come and do the parquet in my house, because they were on very good terms and he did things for him. They got along very well from what I could see. Decent behaviour, invitations to come and have a cup of coffee, and good neighbourly relations between them and the Muslim family -- I mean, from the Josipovic and the Muslim family.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You mentioned Islam Ahmic. What is his ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Islam Ahmic is a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Would you know who were his neighbours? Who were other Muslim neighbours of his?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: I knew a number of people because we went to school together. Rahim Ahmic, Alaga Ahmic. They were my schoolfellows.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: What were the relations between Drago and his neighbours? Do you know Fahrudin Ahmic, for instance?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were on very close terms. I did not meet him particularly, but I heard from what he told me when he would be there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: What you are telling us about Drago Josipovic, that you knew him at work. Yes, of course, naturally you worked there, but after working hours did you ever come closer to his house? How is it that you know him after working hours? Could you tell us something about that?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I would come near his house helping my sister-in-law.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Will you please -- what kind of a sister-in-law?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Sister-in-law is my husband's sister. She had a plot of land. She had some private property and we helped them cultivate it, whatever they -- the crops they grew, that is, maize, potatoes, vegetable garden, and such like.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Right. So you used to go there. Do you remember the first conflict on the 20th of October, 1992? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: No, in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did you hear anything about that?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did hear about it. I was at home on sick leave, and I heard that a conflict had broken out but I wouldn't know any details. I only heard about this and I had no opportunity of learning anything more about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: What did you hear?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: I heard that in the lower area a conflict had broken out, that there was some unrest, that there was some gunfire.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Were any structures damaged about Drago Josipovic?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: I think I heard that mostly structures like stables were damaged, some houses were on fire, but I didn't hear much about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Right. Was Drago Josipovic a member of the HDZ? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think that Drago was a member of the HDZ.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Do you know Slavica Josipovic?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Drago Josipovic's wife. I do know her.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, would you please show the photocopy of this photograph to the witness?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D40/4.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So you have before you this photocopy of the passport with the photograph of Slavica Josipovic. Mrs. Vukadinovic, you have it over there on the ELMO. Would you please look at it there? You can see it better there. Who is this?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: This is Slavica Josipovic from Santici, Drago Josipovic's wife.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. President, we have been referring to Mrs. Slavica Josipovic all the time, that she turned up at the press conference, and there was transmitted by Busovaca TV. I would like to suggest to show the videotape to the witness. This is D34/2. I do not think it will take a long time. I should only like to show the beginning and just to have the witness testify to it and then tender this photograph into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Can we stop here, please? Can we stop here, right at the beginning? Stop right at the beginning to ask the witness if she recognises Slavica Josipovic, and so can we show the tape, the very beginning, so the witness can see if she recognises the person?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: This person that you see in this photograph, is that Slavica Josipovic or not?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: No, this is not Slavica Josipovic. I can affirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Thank you. Do I not need this videotape any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: I shall move on with my questions. Mrs. Vukadinovic, you told us that you came to your sister-in-law, that is your husband's sister, to Santici?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Would you see Drago Josipovic at home often or seldom?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: He was at home mostly. Often.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: How did he go to work?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: He went to work by the company bus. It was organised by the company.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did he ever drive a private car?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: I never saw him drive a private car.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And where did Slavica Josipovic work?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Slavica Josipovic worked in the municipal administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And after that? I mean after 1993?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: I believe she worked for Rajkovic, a private company, and during the war, she worked for the humanitarian cooperative, Mother and Child.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Will you tell us, on what terms did she work, more or less?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Oh, she worked too much. She was just too active at work.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: But did she have any time to devote herself to her home as Drago Josipovic did?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: No. She is a different kind of person. She is always moving about, she is always busy, and she was very socially and publicly active, she worked in the company and did all sorts of other things rather than be at home and engage in household chores.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did Drago and Slavica Josipovic have a car?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did have a car. I think it was a Yugo make, and Slavica took it to go to work.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did she use it outside working hours?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, she did. She always drove it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So she was very busy and she moved about very much, and Drago Josipovic did not.

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: No, Drago did not go out much, but she drove the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You mentioned that Drago Josipovic had a positive attitude to Muslims?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He was a very positive individual indeed in his relations with all people, with Muslims and Serbs and Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did Muslims respect him, bearing in mind that they elected him to union bodies and then to the Workers' Council?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course he was respected, and he was tolerant in his work both in those fora, in those public fora, and at work.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did you ever think that Drago hated Muslims?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: No. He cannot hate anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: We shall move on to another subject but for one question. Some witnesses stated here in court that, on the 16th of March -- of April, '93, early in the morning, that is, at half past 5.00, left his home in the direction of Rovna. Would you know if and when Drago Josipovic left his home and how in the direction of Rovna?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: All I know about these details --

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I must object to this question because I did not know until now that the witness was present in Ahmici on the 16th of April and could tell us anything about what happened in Ahmici on the 16th of April. So I do object to this question. I do not think she can tell us that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes, the Prosecutor is right. This witness was presented as a character witness, not as a fact witness, so if you could please refrain from asking questions about the 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. President, you said that the Chamber could, at its discretion, decide that if it would be in the interests of justice, we can ask some supplementary questions. This is, however, related to Josipovic's character, that is, whether he agreed to participate in fighting or whether he refused to. So I believe my question was a natural, a logical one. How did Drago Josipovic behave that way, how did he act that morning, if she had heard. I only asked her what she had heard. I never asked her or intimated that she had been in Ahmici that morning, and I think that my question was proper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: I'm so sorry, I would like to ask you to move on, to move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: I will rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Do you know if Drago Josipovic took part in the slaying of Muslims and destruction of their houses in view of the kind of man he was?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Susak, of course you cannot put this question. This has nothing to do with the character of Mr. Josipovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Then I will ask just one more question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You said that you came near Drago Josipovic's house, that is, to your husband's sister's house, and when you would be there, would you be afraid if you would see any uniformed men moving in the direction of Novi Travnik, that means how did Drago Josipovic's family feel?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: "At that time." What time do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: '93. I mean the time prior to the second conflict.

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: At that time, I did not go in that direction and I seldom went there because the immediate danger of war had already been proclaimed and a state of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So who used that road; will you just tell us that? Who held it?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, this is the main road. This is the main communication, and at that time, it was regulated by military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have here a list of the HDZ from the 18th of September, '91 until the 8th of April, '92. It has been submitted to the Chamber and to us, and it is assumed that the persons listed here are HDZ members. So can this list be shown to this witness because I shall like to ask her some questions about it?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Mr. Susak, could you please remind us of the number that this exhibit had, the list?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: This is 41. This is going to be 41.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No, it's Exhibit 353.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: But the Prosecutor has already tendered that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Exhibit 353.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Your Honour, no. This is another list.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: This is another list. Three hundred fifty-three is a list of HVO members, and this is a list of HDZ members during the period of time prior to April '92, and we gave it to the Defence because we thought it might be of some help to them, but I do not think that it is already on the records.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is Prosecutor's Exhibit 371.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mrs. Vukodinovic, would you please take this list in your hand, but could you move over so that it can also be seen on the ELMO and you can look at it. Don't look at the monitor, please, but look at the list itself. Could you move your chair so that you can do that? Could you please turn to page 1? Could you tell me what the title means, "Participants in the Armed Resistance to Aggression"?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: When it says "Participants in the Armed Resistance to Aggression," these are mainly men who are of military age, who are able-bodied and able to take part in defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Very well. Could you tell me what it says on the left, at the head?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: It says "Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, the Municipal Head Office in Vitez."

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So this is a list of the Vitez municipality head office?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: On the right-hand side, it says "Basic Branch," and then there is a place name.

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This refers to the territory to which --

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: The local commune?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the local commune belongs to.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: On this list and the other lists, is there any mention of the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: No, not on this page.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Would you please tell us where you are from?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: I was born in Mosunj, the village of Mali Mosunj. I married in Kruscica.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So you married in Kruscica where you live?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I live in Kruscica.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And you were born in Mali Mosunj?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And you were employed in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was employed in Vitez the whole time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Since the list shows the names of people who were, as you said, able-bodied and of military age, I would like to ask you about the people from Kruscica, Mali Mosunj, and the centre of Vitez because these are people you know, taking into account the fact that you were born there or that you lived there or worked there. Could you please find the village of Mali Mosunj here and the persons listed from that village and column 11?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: I found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: What name is written here? We said column number 11.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Susak, do you mean page 11?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Yes. The list is according to places. In the right-hand corner, at the top, is the name of the place.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mrs. Vukodinovic, would you listen to me, please? Could you please look at the first page of the small format and find the column 11. It's page 39. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: What does column 11 say?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Zigonjic Stipe Franjo.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So Franjo, son of Stipe Zigonjic. Was he a member of the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: No, he was not a member of the HDZ, but he was able-bodied and able to take part in defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Would you please find the name Ivan Budimir on this -- number 11 on the big list; 111 but 11 on the big list, Mali Mosunj. It's near the end of the big list.

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: He was a member of the HDZ. He was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Would you please tell us who signed this list?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: The list was signed by all those who happened to be at home when the lists were drawn up.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Who was Ivan Budimir?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Ivan Budimir was a personal friend of mine and an acquaintance.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did he sign this list for Mali Mosunj?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: No, it's not his signature, it's the signature of his wife, Marija.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Why did his wife sign the list instead of him?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Because he was not at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Do you know, in the village of Gacice, if you look at column 11 you can find the name Slavo Krizanovic. Have you found it? The village of Gacice.

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me the page number?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: It's column 7 on the little format, the small format.

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: What page?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: I found it. I found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Slavko Krizanovic. Was he on the list?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Could you tell us the page number? Do you know Susak, we don't have the page number.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecutor did not number the pages, but it's page 34 on the small format. Thirty-nine you said? Could you please help me, because you have it in front of you. What page is it? It's 51. Page 51.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Could you please tell us who signed for Slavko Krizanovic?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: His wife Danica did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Was he a member of the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Slavko is was not a member of the HDZ.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Why did his wife sign his name then?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Because he wasn't at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: We have now a block of last names which you will find easily. It's the municipality centre, the centre of Vitez. Could you please point out the names of people who are not members of the HDZ but whose names are on this list? It's for the centre of Vitez. It's in the middle of the small format. You found it. Could you please list, if you know, the people who are on this list? You can tell us the number. It begins with number 53.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Could you please, again, give us the page number?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is very confused because there are other numbers for every place. It's 74. It's page 74, but for this person it's number 74.

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: This page shows the name of Marinko Katava from the centre Territorial Defence. He was not a member of the HDZ.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Could you turn to the next page and could you tell us who else on this list was not an HDZ member?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Denis Ajanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: What is he by nationality?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: His mother was a Serb and his father was a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Who signed for him? Is this his signature?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: It was signed by his father, Nedzib Ajanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Could you look at number 94 now?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Niko Tihomir Josic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Was he a member?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: He was not a member of the HDZ.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Who signed for him?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: His sister, Dragica Elek.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: We are now going on to page 76. Would you look at number 113? Who is this?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Desimir Skavo.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Rademko?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Rademko, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Was he a member of the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: He was not a member of the HDZ.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: What is he by nationality?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: He is a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Number 116.

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Dusko Bulajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Was he a member of the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: He was not a member of the HDZ.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: What is he by nationality?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: He's a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Now, to cut this short, let us just look at number 130.

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: The name is Milan Subasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: What is he by nationality?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Milan Subasic, is a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Was he a member of the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: No, he wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Could you tell us if this is his signature?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment. Yes, he signed this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Very well. What about Milenko Mirkovic? It's on page 77, number 141.

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Was he a member of the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Could you tell us who signed for him? Is this his signature? It doesn't say "Milenko."

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: I think it was signed by Madam Ljilja.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: He is a Serb by nationality?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Then you have Predrag Todorovic. What is he by nationality?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: He was Serb by nationality.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did he sign this himself? Is this his signature or is this a different name?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: No, it wasn't him. It was his wife.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And last -- we're still on the same page, 77, in column 146 or, rather, in line 146, Pero Knezic. What was he by nationality?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: He was a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Was he a member of the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Could you tell me whether there were any Serbs in Vitez who were members of the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: No, there weren't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Because they had the SDS party and most of them belonged to that party.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So they had their own ethnic party?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They also had the SDP party in which most -- so most Serbs were either in the SDP or the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Could you tell us how this list was drawn up, if you know? You said that you're a lawyer.

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So who drew up this list and in what way, if you know? I would like to draw your attention to the signatories, coordinator, commander, and the president of the branch of the HDZ. So do you know how this list was drawn up?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know how it was drawn up. At the initiative of the HDZ, the list was started in municipal head office. One of the members was from the HDZ. The second member was from the office for defence, and the third member of the group drawing up the list was someone who coordinated their work with the municipal head office and the defence office, because this had to do with the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So you want to tell us that these three signatories, the three people who drew up this list were the coordinator, the commander, and the head of the local branch. So there was one member of the HDZ, one representative of defence office, and the third one was a representative of the territory, of the -- so can you tell us what the role of the HDZ was here?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: The HDZ took the initiative in all this so that a list would be drawn up by territorial branches, because the HDZ organised itself along territorial lines. So that made it easier to get hold of information.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So they gave information to the office for defence.

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but I have to stress that only one of the people who did this was a member of the HDZ.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: This was always the president of the local branch of the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: I would now like to ask you -- you have seen the list and we have pointed out several persons who were not members of the HDZ, so I would now like to ask you the following: Were all the persons on this list members of the HDZ or were only some of them members of the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: As I have already said, these are only persons who are able-bodied and of military age, and there are HDZ members among them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: The signatories who sign this list, if you look at page 1, did they know were signing -- were they aware of the fact that they were signing this as HDZ members or as participants in organised resistance?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: No. They knew they were signing only as participants of organised resistance to aggression.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So they did not know that this list was an HDZ list because it doesn't say that anywhere?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: But this is not an HDZ list.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. President, Mr. Susak is asking the witness to say something about persons who are registered here, and a number of them. I do not think that these questions are particularly relevant, and he is either asking the witness something that he can say or, again, the witness should tell us under what circumstances and how did she learn about the conditions and about people who signed this list, otherwise, I do not think that we can come to a point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Susak, I think the Prosecutor is right. So could you please either refrain from asking this question or rephrase it along the lines suggested by the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: I'll ask what does "Local branch" mean here in the heading? What does it say here? There's a place name but is the HDZ mentioned anywhere here on the document?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: In the left-hand corner at the top, it just says "Local branch."

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You mean the right-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I mean the right-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Does it say that this is a local branch of the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: No. No, it doesn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: What does this mean? Is this the territorial principle, according to which information was provided for certain people from a certain territory for the needs of the defence office?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. So this is simply of territorial importance. It shows where these people are, to which territory they belong.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did HDZ members have documents showing that they were HDZ members?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: If they had been listed as HDZ members, would the number of the document have been entered in here?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. It's logical.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Another question: At that time, in 1991 and 1992, did the Croats know or, rather, did you know that in 1993 there was going to be a conflict between the Muslims and the Croats?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: At that time, no one thought there might be a conflict between the Croats and the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So on this list we see that the list is participants in organised resistance to aggression. Every page is the same. Could you look at page 1? Is this what people signed, "Participants in organised assistance to aggression?"

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Mostly they signed this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: This has been delivered to us by the Prosecution as a cover page, and it says "HDZ," from the period of a certain date to -- from the 18th of September, 1991, to the 8th of April, 1992. What does this mean?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: This was all prepared for the Vitez defence office, and this shows that one of the people drawing up this list was an HDZ member, because the initiative came from HDZ members to complete the job faster and to complete the organisation by territorial branches.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: These HDZ territorial branches, did they have the best information because other authorities were not functioning considering the war?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, considering there was a state of immediate threat of war, the HDZ had the best territorial organisation and that is why this activity was started, according to the territorial branches.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Do you know, at the railway station, which is a part of Vitez, one of the people who signed this list is Dragan Strbac. Can you tell me who he was?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Dragan Strbac was working in the Civil Defence, cooperating with the Defence office, or, rather, this was part of the Defence Office of Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: It means that Dragan Strbac was a coordinator. Do you know of any other instance when coordinators turned up and they worked for the defence office?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: There is also Zdravko Bosnjak who still works for the Defence Office in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did he also sign as a coordinator?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Both as a coordinator or as a member, depending on where he worked.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: As three persons invariably signed these lists, the coordinator, representative of the basic branch of the HDZ, were they always HDZ members or not?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: We have the chairman of the basic branch. He was also the president of the HDZ for this basic branch.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And the other two coordinators?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: They did not have to be members of the HDZ. They be could simply activists of the Civil Defence or the Defence Office in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have no more questions. I should also like to tender into evidence D39 and D40.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Any objection? No objection. They are admitted into evidence. Mr. Terrier?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Good morning, Madam. My name is Franck Terrier, and I represent the Prosecution. I would like to ask you several questions on the basis of your testimony. First I should like to ask you if you are related to Dragan Vukodinovic, who was the president of the Vitez HDZ.

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Dragan Vukodinovic is my late husband.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Can you confirm that he was a member of the Vitez HDZ?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I confirm that he was a member of the Vitez HDZ.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: And you yourself, were you a member of the HDZ party during the period concerned, that is, in '91, '92, and '93?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: I was not a member of the HDZ or any other political party.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Is it absurd to think that even if not a member of the HDZ, you nevertheless were very interested in the work of this organisation because you could offer us very accurate information about the conditions under which this list was compiled? Mr. Susak has an objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. President, I abide by your written instructions. I think that the Prosecution has now gone beyond the examination-in-chief, because during the examination-in-chief, I never mentioned Mrs. Vukodinovic's husband.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: But the question has nothing to do with the testimony, that is, the position of the witness in the HDZ. If she knew, if she had information, even if she was not a member of the HDZ, she nevertheless evidently knew, had information about the organisation, about the functioning of that party, so I think the question is pertinent.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Madam, how did you learn about the internal organisation of the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was like this: I was a direct member of the election committee and I had all the information related to the elections of '92 accessible to me so I didn't go into that. I was not biased, I did not support any of these parties, I was not interested in any -- particularly any detail regarding any party active in the Vitez territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: A few moments ago, in answer to Mr. Susak's question, you told us who was a member of the HDZ and who was not a member of the HDZ on this list and under what conditions this list was compiled, so apparently you know very well how the HDZ in Vitez worked, not only how it worked but also who were its members. So my question is: How could you acquire this particular knowledge that you shared with us a few moments ago?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: I did not have to gather that particular knowledge anywhere because I live and work in Vitez and I was, as of the beginning, informed about the situation in Vitez as a member of the election commission.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Yes, Madam, but you just told us that this election -- that this commission did not give or have any particular information about the functioning, about the workings of any particular party.

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Right, any party.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Nevertheless, you can tell us, for instance, that Franjo Zigonjic and others were not members of the HDZ. So in what way did you learn that?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Because I only mentioned the names of people I know personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Your husband, did he hold office in the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Until '98, he did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Were you related to Perica Vukodinovic?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Through my marriage.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Could you please explain what you mean?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: They are my husband's relations.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I ask you because a witness who testified here on the 11th of February, '98 [sic], a Defence witness, mentioned the name of Perica Vukodinovic as implicated in the murder of Samir Trako in Vitez in May 1992, but you are not personally related to this individual, are you?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Whom do you mean, Perica Vukodinovic or Samir?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Perica Vukodinovic.

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I know him rather well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: What do you know about the incident with Samir that I mentioned?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Very little.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is really going beyond the framework of the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. President, yes, that is quite true, but nevertheless it is very difficult to know what are the boundaries of the examination-in-chief because what he was asking had nothing to do with examination-in-chief before. But I shall move on to another question, and I hope that the witness will be able to tell us -- I hope that the witness will be able to give us some information about this incident, but nevertheless ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Madam, I believe you can tell us if Drago Josipovic was a member of the HDZ, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: You seem to have closely read this list. Does Drago Josipovic figure in it?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Could you tell us the page -- could you indicate the page -- oh, it is --

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, if I look at it, because they were compiled per branch offices, that is, per territory, and I can say that this was the territory of Santici.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Will you please tell us the page number?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Page 19. Forty-five. He's under number 45.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Thank you. And this signatory who signed for that name, is that Drago Josipovic's signature? Was it signed by Drago Josipovic as far as you can tell us?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is his signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: The presence of Drago Josipovic's name on this list and his signature here, does that not mean that he was a member of the HDZ at that time? And we're talking about the 18th of September, '91 until the 8th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: The fact that Drago Josipovic's name features on this list and the fact that he signed this list personally, it says HDZ, between the -- in the list which says HDZ, between the 18th of September, '91 and the 8th of April, '92, does that not mean that Drago Josipovic was a member of the HDZ during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: It need not mean that. It can only mean that he happened to be at home at the time when they were drawing up this list.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: You said at home. Was he at home or without work? Did he just happen to be at home when these people happened to be passing by? What do you mean when you say he was at home?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: That at the time, when this list was being drawn up, when the names were collected, he happened to be at home. It need not mean that there were not any other persons, but it is most proper for the person whose particulars have been taken to sign the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I understand. What you are saying is that he was at home and people came and asked him to sign and he signed. But why is his name on this list? Why was his name put on this list?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Because he was either able-bodied, that is, he could work or he would fight. He was of military age and able-bodied.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: But don't we see on this list all the people from the territory of Vitez who are able-bodied and are of military age? And that is not the case. We don't have the list of all the people fitting that description.

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: But these are the initial data found there, that is my guess, at the time when these lists were made on the basis of the territorial principle.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Madam, another document was tendered here under P353, and this is a list of names of people who participated in the defence during the period after April 1992, and that list and other lists include many more names; it is two or three times as long as this list here. So does it not -- so that this list is not the same as the list which is numbered 353, and the list which you have before you, is it not a selection of certain names because this list does not include the names of all the inhabitants of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: It need not mean that because this is not an official census. The official census or official list was kept only by the authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I shall move on to another question. You spoke about Drago Josipovic's wife, Slavica. Did you maintain any personal relations with her?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: No, not at that time. My relations were with Drago and it had to do with our work. I knew Slavica only through administration bodies, that is, because of work, and I didn't know her as much as I knew Drago.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: But didn't you tell us a moment ago that you visited Drago Josipovic professionally and also privately, that is, both during working hours and outside working hours, and that you also were informed about his personal life, you knew about his private life, about his children?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, because we met often, and in the course of our conversations, we got to know one another and children and wife, that is, I met his wife through him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I see. But you did not know his wife personally.

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, through him and through work.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I believe there is some -- I think we are talking at cross-purposes. But did you go to his house? Have you been to his home?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: I was invited there only when we worked at my husband's sister's, next to his home, so they would invite us over for a friendly chat at times when we would take rest.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: So did you meet his wife on such occasions?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Not very often. Slavica usually was not at home but Drago and his late mother were very considerate, very hospitable, and on such occasions, yes, I met Slavica outside work.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: But tell us when it was that you met Slavica? Was it in 1993 or before that?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Before 1993, I met her through work. She was the one who issued building permits. She worked at the office for the issuance of building permits and worked in the enterprise. Then I would ask Drago something else, whatever we needed for the company, anything that we needed, and he told us that his wife worked there and so it was easier to solve some company matters through her. But it was prior to 1990, it was before 1990 even.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: But at that time, Slavica Josipovic was not often at home, as you told us, and is it because she had some political duties, because she held some political office?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Not at that time. She only was employed and worked for the administration, but she would go out into the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Could you be more specific? What period of time are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Before 1990.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: If we then turn to the period after 1990, that is, 1991 principally until 1993, at that time, could you then answer my question regarding the political work of Slavica?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: All I know is that Slavica was a member of the HDZ, but whether she held some office there, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: You can tell us who is and who is not a member of the HDZ in this list. We could see that. But you cannot tell us what were the responsibilities, what were the duties of Slavica Josipovic in the HDZ, can you?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that. As far as I know, as of 1995, she may have had some office, that is, after the ceasefire was signed in '94, that is, '95, I believe she was on the municipal board, but during that period of time, I'm not really -- I don't think she held any particular office.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: A moment ago you told us that Drago Josipovic held some union positions, that he was representing the unions at the Sintevit company and two other companies. Could you tell us, how did he come to hold those offices? Was it through appointment or through election?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: It was like this -- it would take a great long time to describe to you the sort of management system arrangements, when you have workers' assemblies pronouncing themselves someplace. "Workers' assembly" means all employees of a production plant. They would nominate one or two persons from amongst themselves to the executive board. Then this executive board of the union would then elect their representatives to the action conference, that is, all production units would nominate their representatives. So he had to be nominated by somebody from his own production plant.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: So to try to make it as clear as possible, and this is something that does not exist any more, but you are telling us that he was nominated for this office, for this post?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, somebody had to nominate him. The constituency, so to speak, were the body of employees, that is, somebody had to nominate him and he would be elected. He was on the list. There would be a secret ballot usually, but at times they would also vote publicly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: As of when did Drago Josipovic come to hold these executive posts in the union, these offices in the union?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, those were not professional posts. We call them self-management offices. So he did not do it professionally. He was not paid for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: But my question is: When is it that Drago Josipovic was elected to these offices that you just described to us?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot remember exactly. I do know that before 1990 he already was nominated. First they would be elected for a four-year term, then they were elected for a two-year term. So I cannot say. So it would be 1988 until 1990 he was a member of the executive board. After '91, I really cannot say without some reliable proof.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: But the same set of documents which Mr. Susak submitted awhile ago were talking about the beginning, the early days of 1991.

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That documents referred to 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I mean that before that. Drago Josipovic did not hold any noteworthy office prior to 1991?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's what is I said. I confirmed that because I worked as of 1991. As of '91, I was on leave because I was expecting a baby, so that for other periods of time I can speak only on the basis of some documentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Now I'm referring to 1991, '92, and '93. During that period of time, the question of political membership, partisanship, would it affect, of course -- would it affect the membership in the union or the posts held there, or some management bodies?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: No. Union organisations had never anything to do with political membership.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: But the political conflict, did it affect somehow the union movement, the union structure?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: There were no political conflicts at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: After the elections, after the big elections, but this is a question which does not refer to Drago Josipovic specifically but the existence of different parties, some of them were very ethnically based, such as HDZ, SDS, and so on and so forth. Did this aspect affect the unions in any manner, the institutional organisation of unions? Do you understand my questions?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: No, union worked independent of party membership during that period of time. During that period of time, their activity came down only to the distribution of relief, provision of food supplies for the employees.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Could you tell us what period of time you are talking about?

utterances.speaker: MILICA VUKADINOVIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about the time after 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. We will take a break now? Before we take a break, Mr. Susak, do you have many questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: No, do I not, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: No questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. President, excuse me, has this book been tendered into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: The list you mean, the register?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: She said it was 371.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: I think it should be. It should be given a number. 371, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I tender it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: No objection, Counsel Susak, for the 371?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. President, I've object to its being admitted into evidence because the title has been added to these lists, and the title does not correspond with the contents of this list because these people are not HDZ members. So I object to its being admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: On the other hand, Counsel Susak, this was relied upon by you yourself. It was not produced by the Prosecutor. It was handed by the Prosecutor to the Defence counsel, and you quoted and actually heavily relied on this document. How can you now object to its admission into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. President, I hope you will see my point. This is the last witness for Drago Josipovic and I had to ask these questions, but I do not know how the Prosecutor will use this document in the future. This was my last opportunity to check on this list. Today I did not intend to tender it into evidence. All I wanted to do was to examine this witness, but the Prosecutor could examine his witnesses in a different manner with regard to this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Well, we admit this document into evidence as P371. All right. Mrs. Vukadinovic, thank you so much for testifying here in The Hague. You may now be released.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: We adjourn for 30 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: I understand a closed session has been requested by Counsel Pavkovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Katava. Would you please stand and make the solemn declaration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated. Counsel Pavkovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Katava.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: It is usual, so would you please first tell us something about yourself, your full name, date of birth?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KATAVA
utterances.text: My name is Marinko Katava. I was born on the 18th of November, 1952, in Busovaca. I live in Vitez. My address is Marshal Tito A5.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Katava, are you married?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Yes. I am married and I have five children.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: What is your wife's name?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KATAVA
utterances.text: My wife is Jelica. My daughters are Anita, Ivana, Kristina, Gabrella.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us how old your children are?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KATAVA
utterances.text: My eldest daughter was born in 1975. The next one in '78. Then we had twins in 1980 and the youngest was born in 1988.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Katava, could you tell me what your profession is?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KATAVA
utterances.text: I am an administrative lawyer and I have been employed in that capacity since 1977.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me what you are doing today?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Today I'm the director of a private company.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any brothers?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Yes. I have a brother who is two years older than me. At the moment he's a refugee from Vukovar, living in the vicinity of Vinkovci.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you speak a little slower because of the interpreters, please? Could you tell me whether you have any half brothers?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Yes, I have two half brothers. They are younger than me. One was born in 1958, the other in 1961.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have a twin brother perhaps?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KATAVA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know -- you say that you are an administrative lawyer by profession. Do you know whether in Vitez and the surrounding area there is another person called Marinko Katava?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Not in Vitez. In 1990, I was a member of the municipal electoral commission and I had a list of the voters, and the only person whose last name was Katava was I. There is another person, much younger than me, called Marinko Katava in the Busovaca municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Today, Mr. Katava, you said that you were the managing director or the owner of a private company. Is it your company?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Yes. It belongs to me and my wife.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: If we go back a little to a time before these wartime events, could you please tell me what you were doing before 1990, what your job was?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Before what year?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: 1990. Were you employed as a lawyer?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Yes. I was employed as a lawyer from the 1st of February, 1987. I was in a timber company called Impregnacia in Vitez, which employed between 500 and 600 employees, and until 1993 I was the head of the personnel department and the general administration department.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me what your job consisted of?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Well, in the self-management system which we had in the entire ex-Yugoslavia, it was a very demanding job. We had to provide services to all the self-management bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: At that time, was the issue of employment and dismissal a topical one?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Yes. I was in charge of all the rights and obligations arising from employment, the start and termination of employment, and in labour disputes and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. After I ask you a question, could you pause a little before replying so that everything you say can be interpreted? In your former job, were you also in charge of resolving the housing problems of the employees?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Yes. In that system, companies had to earmark some of their funds for housing construction. This was a solidarity housing, and every year there were a few flats, the construction of which was funded by our company and which were intended for our employees who had to compete for them at a public competition.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: I would now like to ask you about the names of certain persons, and I would like you to tell me whether they were then employed in your company. Could you tell me whether you knew Muzafer Puscul?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I knew him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Where was he employed?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KATAVA
utterances.text: He worked in Impregnacia, with a secondary school education, as a technician, and he was the foreman. He was the foreman of a shift, and that was a lower level of leadership responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: What were your relations then?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Well, normal, I would say. Nothing special. Neither good nor bad. There were 600 people there. I knew most of them, and they probably all knew me because I was the only person doing my job in that company.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me whether there was an employee called Sakib Ahmic in your company?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Where was Mr. Sakib Ahmic from. Where did he live at that time?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KATAVA
utterances.text: I don't know where he lived -- because I know that he lived in Ahmici. I don't know where in Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me what jobs he did at Impregnacija?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KATAVA
utterances.text: He was the driver of a passenger car and he -- he was the driver for the directors, and the directors had to be re-elected every four years.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: You said that there were numerous employees in your former company. I have asked you about only two of them. I will not go on. Can you just tell me -- please don't mention any third names -- but between the two persons we have mentioned, was there any connection, and if so, what kind of connection was there between Muzafer Puscul and Sakib Ahmic?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Muzafer was Sakib's son-in-law.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me, as regards Mr. Sakib Ahmic, one more thing. You said that among your other duties at that time, you were also in charge of the housing problems of your employees. Can you recall an event which might be important today when we mention the name of Mr. Sakib Ahmic or his son-in-law? There is something that I would like to throw light on so it will become clear.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Well, there were several events connected with that family and their housing problems. In those 15 years, there was never a competition for the awarding of an apartment or a loan without their competing. If you will allow me, I would like to tell you two, I might call them anecdotes, from the self-management system. Sakib Ahmic asked for a flat every year, trying to prove that his house had such bad living conditions that he could no longer live in it. When, finally, he managed to get to the top of the list, it was for a one-room apartment, he gave up his position because his son-in-law was the second on the list, so his son-in-law got that apartment. In time, he completed the construction of his family house, but he never gave back the flat to the company. Another thing that happened with regard to Sakib: When he had to prove that he was an employee who was without a place to live in, which would mean that he would get 200 points on that list, he brought along a judgement saying that he was divorced. It was an official court document showing that he was divorced, that he had left his house to his wife and that he was homeless. I'm just trying to show you the character of this man. The president of the housing commission, who had the last say, was Sakib Ahmic's brother, Islam Ahmic, but he then would not allow him to get the apartment by such fraudulent means.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You have given your evaluation of his attitude to these issues, so I will not go on with this line of questioning. Mr. Katava, I would now like to ask you very briefly to recall the beginning of the year 1990 and the time of the major social and political changes that took place then, the time of multi-party elections, and I would like to ask you whether you, at that time, were a member of any political organisation, a political party?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KATAVA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: This means that you were not a member then and you are not a member now of the ruling party, the Croatian Democratic Union --

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KATAVA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: -- the HDZ? With respect to your social activities at that time, can you tell me whether you were a member of some kind of non-political organisation?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Well, I was a member of the hunting association for some 15 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean -- you say 15 years. Starting from when?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Well, 15 years back from now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that you had weapons?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Yes. I had and I still have a hunting rifle produced in the Czech Republic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever have a military weapon so you know how to handle a hunting rifle?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Yes, a hunting rifle, which includes a hunter's carbine, I did not have one but I knew how to use it. I had an old M-48 rifle when I served in the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KATAVA
utterances.text: That was in 1971.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: 1971, yes. Mr. Katava, you told us today where you live, what your address is. Could you tell me, in the first half of 1993, where did you live then?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KATAVA
utterances.text: I lived where I still live, in the same flat, the same address. It was in Vitez, the street was then called Marshal Tito, House number 5. The name of the street was changed after the war, but it is still the same address.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: So in the first half of 1993, and this includes the 16th of April, 1993, your address was Marshal Tito Street, A5?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: And you lived there with your family?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: I would now like to ask you some concrete questions. I have awakened your recollections, so could you please try to remember what you were doing on the 15th of April, 1993, the day before these conflicts broke out?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KATAVA
utterances.text: It was a normal working day like any other, like the 13th, like the 12th, like the 5th, all the days are the same. I would get up at half past six, take my youngest daughter to kindergarten, work from 7.00 to 3.00, then pick up my daughter from the kindergarten, come home. I have children, so that was my daily routine.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: In the afternoon and in the evening, can you remember, for example, when you went to bed?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KATAVA
utterances.text: It was usually after the news at 10 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: And the numerous family members that you mentioned, were they all with you then?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Yes, they were all with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: The children were very young then.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Yes. My eldest daughter was 18. The others were much younger. The youngest was five.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: I would now like to go back to a question, but I will mention the names of some protected witnesses, so I would like to go into private session very briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
